docs.title: Home
docs.text:
NBE ALM Simulation Center

A what-if engine for Asset-Liability Management. Pick a scenario, see the impact on earnings, funding cost and liquidity, and read a management explanation, all computed by deterministic Python on the bank's own positions, cash flows and market data.

Prototype · Version 2.1.0 · Engine v2 9scenario drivers 15KPIs compared 7 + 2tables + SQL views 3report formats 0numbers from the AI

Prototype status

This is a prototype with an NBE-inspired visual theme. It is not an official National Bank of Egypt application, and the figures it produces are analytical proxies, not accounting or regulatory numbers.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Scenario → impact → insight

    Choose a template, set up to nine drivers (policy rate, FX, gold, deposit run-off, loan and deposit growth, inflation, unemployment, GDP) and read the result on one dashboard.

  • Event-based repricing engine

    Interest is computed per position over the chosen horizon. A rate shock only bites after each position's first repricing date inside the window.

  • P&L and value impact

    NII change, macro credit cost, FX and gold revaluation, and investment mark-to-market are combined into one pre-tax proxy.

  • Self-checking

    An independent validation table recomputes NII, NIM, cost of funds, P&L and LCR from the position detail and reports PASS or FAIL.

  • Local AI, explanation only

    Phi-3 through Ollama explains the computed results and parses free-text scenarios. It never calculates a number.

  • Reports

    Download PDF, PowerPoint or a ZIP bundle, plus Excel with live formulas and CSV extracts.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
1. Deterministic numbers. Every figure comes from Python code and can be reproduced. The AI only explains.
  2. Existing database, no DDL. The application reads and writes data rows. It never creates or alters tables.
  3. One consistent currency. FX and gold positions are valued to EGP by the SQL views using the latest market rates, so every amount in the app is an EGP equivalent.
  4. Transparent assumptions. Conventions, thresholds and coefficients are in config.py and explained in these pages, including what the model does not cover. See Limitations.
  5. Graceful degradation. If the database, Ollama or the reporting libraries are unavailable, the rest of the application keeps working and says what is missing.

docs.title: AI Assistant
docs.text:
The application uses a local language model (Phi-3 through Ollama) for exactly two jobs. It never calculates, and no data leaves the machine.

Job Function Input Output Explain a result ask_ollama JSON payload of computed results Executive text, four sections Read a free-text scenario parse_free_type_scenario_with_ollama A sentence Numeric driver values

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.text: Guardrail How Python owns every number The prompt says: do NOT change, invent, or calculate new numerical values Explanation is read-only The model receives results and returns text; nothing is fed back into the engine Deterministic output Temperature is OLLAMA_TEMPERATURE (default 0.0) for explanations and 0 for parsing Parsing is shown before use Extracted values are displayed in a table and clamped by the UI before running Graceful failure If Ollama is down or the model is missing, a message is shown and regex parsing takes over Local only Default endpoint http://localhost:11434

docs.title: Prompt
docs.text: The system role is a Senior ALM Analyst at NBE. The model must return four sections: Executive Summary, Key Financial Drivers, Risk & Liquidity Impact, Strategic ALCO Recommendations. It is told to base everything strictly on the JSON.

docs.title: Payload sent to the model
docs.text:
Field Content Identity Scenario name, type, simulation date, horizon inputs The nine driver values before, after All KPI dictionaries (macro fields removed) risk, overall_risk Risk summary rows and the overall level deterministic_insights The rule-based sentences

Saved explanations are loaded from the database the next time the same scenario is opened, so the model is called once per run.

docs.title: Free-text parsing
docs.text:
1. If Ollama is running and the model is installed, Phi-3 is asked for JSON with the nine keys (format: json).
  2. Values go through clean_numeric_value, which understands bps (divides by 100).
  3. A regex parser (English and Arabic) fills any key the model left empty.
  4. The result records its source, phi3 or regex_fallback.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Set in Data & Settings → AI (Ollama) or through OLLAMA_HOST, OLLAMA_MODEL, OLLAMA_TIMEOUT (default 800 s) and OLLAMA_TEMPERATURE. Any Ollama model name can be used, though the prompt was written for Phi-3.

docs.title: Choosing the model
docs.text:
Option Trade-off Phi-3 (current) Small, runs on a laptop, keeps data local; weaker prose and occasional drift from the payload Larger local model Better narrative, needs more memory Hosted model Best quality, but requires approval to send bank data outside

Because the model never produces numbers, swapping it changes only the wording quality, not the results.

docs.title: Reviewing AI text
docs.text: AI explanations are drafts. Before circulation, an analyst should check that every figure quoted matches the KPI table, which is straightforward because the same payload is available on the dashboard.

docs.title: Analytics & Validation
docs.text: analytics.py turns engine output into tables a person can read, a risk rating, and an independent check. It never changes a number; it only recombines.

docs.title: KPI comparison
docs.text:
comparison_table produces the 15 KPIs compared on the dashboard.

Source KPIs Unit Positions NII, Loans, Deposits, Funding, Investments, Repricing Gap EGP Positions NIM %, Cost of Funds %, Loan Deposit % % Cash flows Liquidity (net cash flow) EGP Cash flows CF LCR % % P&L Credit Cost, FX Gold Revaluation, Investment MTM, Total Impact EGP

Columns: Before, After, Absolute Change, Change % (change over the absolute base value).

docs.title: Risk summary
docs.text:
build_alm_risk_summary rates five indicators.

Indicator Rule NII, NIM ADVERSE if lower, POSITIVE if higher Cost of funds ADVERSE if higher, POSITIVE if lower Repricing gap Informational LCR proxy HIGH if below the limit (LCR_WARNING_THRESHOLD, default 100), otherwise OK

docs.title: Overall risk rating
docs.text:
overall_risk_rating starts at LOW and raises the level when any rule fires. Each rule adds a reason string shown on the dashboard.

Rule Threshold (config.py) Result LCR proxy below limit 100 HIGH NII change ≤ −10 % HIGH NII change ≤ −3 % MEDIUM Total P&L impact as % of base NII ≤ −10 % HIGH Total P&L impact as % of base NII ≤ −3 % MEDIUM Cost of funds up by ≥ 50 bps MEDIUM LCR relative drop ≤ −25 % MEDIUM

The final rating is the highest level reached. Thresholds are constants and LCR_WARNING_THRESHOLD can be set with an environment variable.

LCR rule and the base case

Because the LCR proxy is HQLA divided by deposits, it can sit below 100 % even in the base case, which makes the rating HIGH regardless of the scenario. Verify on real data, and consider recalibrating the limit or the definition.

docs.title: Management insights
docs.text: management_insights writes four sentences from the numbers (NII with rate and volume effects, NIM and cost of funds in bps, liquidity, total impact). It is template text, not AI, and is the fallback explanation in reports.

docs.title: Driver attribution
docs.text:
driver_attribution answers which driver caused how much of the effect.

  1. Run the combined scenario.
  2. For each non-zero driver, run it alone with every other driver neutral.
  3. Report each driver's NII impact and total P&L impact.
  4. Report an Interaction row.
\[\text{Interaction} = (\text{Combined} - \text{Base}) - \sum_{drivers} (\text{Standalone} - \text{Base})\]

A non-zero interaction means the drivers amplify or offset each other, for example a balance-growth effect multiplied by a rate effect. The last row repeats the combined result so the table adds up. Results are cached for 120 seconds per scenario.

docs.title: Other analytics
docs.text: Function Output shock_sensitivity Re-runs the engine over a list of shock values for one driver position_sensitivity Top 10 positions by absolute total impact (NII impact + valuation + MTM − credit cost) pnl_components The four P&L components for the waterfall chart liquidity_ladder Inflow, outflow, net and cumulative net by maturity bucket (0-7, 8-30, 31-90, 91-180, 181-365 days, over 1 year) exposure_tables Balances and interest before and after, grouped by category, currency and product family build_data_quality_checks Row counts and source notes (its tab is hidden in v2.1)

docs.title: Independent validation
docs.text:
calculation_validation_table recomputes headline numbers directly from the position-level detail and compares them with the reported KPIs.

Check Formula NII (before) Σ asset interest − Σ liability interest, before NII (after) The same, after NII change Equals rate effect + volume effect NIM (after) NII × 365/H ÷ (loans + investments) × 100 Cost of funds (after) Interest expense × 365/H ÷ (deposits + funding) × 100 Total impact ΔNII − credit cost + revaluation + MTM LCR CF HQLA ÷ deposits × 100

Each row shows Expected, Actual, Difference and PASS, FAIL or SKIP with tolerances of 0.01 EGP for amounts and 0.0001 for percentages.

What validation proves

The check confirms that the summary layer agrees with the position layer. It is a consistency test, not an external reconciliation to the general ledger or to a regulatory report. It also cannot catch a conceptual error that is present in both places.

docs.title: Row-by-Row table and Excel
docs.text: build_full_row_by_row_scenario_table builds one wide row per position (inputs, scenario parameters, isolated effects). export_row_by_row_with_formulas_xlsx writes it with Excel formulas so every effect can be traced. See the caveat in Reports & Exports.

docs.title: Request lifecycle
docs.text:
Streamlit re-runs the script on every interaction. Each run does the following.

sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant UI as ui.py
    participant DB as database.py
    participant C as calculations.py
    participant P as Page module
    participant A as analytics.py
    U->>UI: interaction
    UI->>DB: connect_existing_database()
    DB-->>UI: engine (tables validated)
    UI->>DB: cached_alm_data() (TTL 120 s)
    DB-->>UI: flat positions, flat cash flows, market data, history
    UI->>C: prepare_inputs(positions, cashflows, market)
    C-->>UI: prep (normalized positions, cash flows, macro snapshot)
    UI->>P: page(ctx, history)
    P->>C: apply_prepared(prep, date, horizon, params)
    C-->>P: before KPIs, after KPIs, position detail
    P->>A: comparison, risk, validation, attribution
    A-->>P: tables
    P->>DB: persist_simulation() on "Run & save"

The shared context ctx (a SimpleNamespace) carries the engine, raw tables, the flat views, the prepared inputs, a data stamp used as a cache key, and the saved scenario history.

docs.title: Execution flow of a scenario
docs.text:
run_scenario() in ui_common.py is the single entry point used by every page:

  1. build_scenario_parameters fills missing drivers with neutral defaults.
  2. apply_prepared runs the position engine and the liquidity engine and returns before, after and the position-level detail.
  3. comparison_table, build_alm_risk_summary and overall_risk_rating build the result tables.
  4. calculation_validation_table recomputes the headline KPIs independently.

    Q -- no --> R[Regex parser]

The model does two things only: it extracts explicit numbers from text, and it narrates results that Python already computed. See AI Assistant.

docs.title: Deployment shape
docs.text: A single Streamlit process, one MySQL database and an optional local Ollama service. There is no application server, message queue or external API. This keeps data on the bank's own machines.

docs.title: Calculation Engine
docs.text:
All numbers in the application come from calculations.py. This page lists every formula in the order the engine applies it. Symbols: \(b_0\) balance before, \(b_1\) balance after, \(r_0\) rate before, \(r_1\) rate after, \(D\) accrual days, \(H\) horizon days, \(t_1\) days from the simulation date to the first repricing event.

Conventions

Rates are decimal fractions (0.12 = 12 %). Day count is actual/365 (DAYS_PER_YEAR). Amounts are EGP equivalents. Interest is accrued over the horizon, not annualised, unless a formula says so.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[Flat views] --> B[normalize_positions / normalize_cashflows]
    B --> C[prepare_inputs<br/>q0, cash flows, valuation date, macro snapshot]
    C --> D[run_position_engine<br/>per position]
    D --> E[summarize_positions<br/>Before and After KPIs]
    D --> F[cashflow_metrics<br/>liquidity and LCR proxy]
    E --> G[apply_prepared<br/>adds P&L components, effects, macro block]
    F --> G
    G --> H[before, after, position detail]

prepare_inputs does the normalisation that does not depend on the scenario once per page run, and the resulting prep object is reused by every scenario evaluation on that run (the dashboard, sensitivity and attribution), so those repeated engine runs do not re-normalise the data.

docs.title: 1. Classification
docs.text: Rule Detail Active only Positions whose Status is Active or blank Category ALM_Position_Category title-cased: Loan, Deposit, Investment, other Funding A Deposit whose segment is in FUNDING_SEGMENTS (Treasury) becomes Funding Balance Evaluated_Balance_EGP, or native balance × market rate when missing Frequency days Text such as Monthly is mapped by FREQUENCY_WORD_DAYS (30, 91, 182, 365...). Codes like 3M use TENOR_DAY_FACTORS (M = 30.4375). At Maturity, Spot, Open-ended have no frequency

docs.title: 2. Accrual window
docs.text:
\[h_{end} = sim + H\]
  • A position is matured if its maturity date is on or before the simulation date. It is excluded (balance set to 0, days 0) because EXCLUDE_MATURED_POSITIONS = True.
  • With ROLLOVER_AT_MATURITY = True every surviving position accrues for the whole horizon: \(D = H\). A position maturing inside the window is assumed to roll over.

docs.title: 3. Repricing event
docs.text:
A position is rate-eligible when its rate type is not fixed / non-interest / zero interest and is floating-like, or when its category is loan, deposit, funding or investment. In practice almost every non-fixed position is eligible.

First event date.

  • Take Next_Repricing_Date.
  • If it is before the simulation date, roll it forward by whole frequency steps: \(\lceil (sim - rep) / f \rceil\) days. If there is no frequency, use the simulation date.
  • If the date is blank, the first event is the simulation date.

Event exists (has_event, shown as the Eligible column) when \(D>0\) and either

  • the position is eligible and its first event is before the end of the window, or
  • it is not eligible (fixed) but matures inside the window, so it reprices at maturity.
\[t_1 = \min\big(\max(first - sim, 0),\ D\big)\] Output Meaning Repricing Event Count 0 without an event; else the number of frequency steps after the first, rounded up, or 1 Repricing Fraction \((D - t_1)/D\), the share of the window spent at the new rate

The column called Eligible

It means has a repricing event inside the horizon, not is floating-rate. This is the set used by the repricing gap.

docs.title: 4. Rate shock
docs.text:
Only a parallel shock exists.

\[\Delta r = \frac{rate\_change\_pp}{100}\] \[r_1 = \begin{cases} \max(0,\ r_0 + \Delta r) & \text{if the position has an event} \\ r_0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}\]

The floor RATE_FLOOR is 0. There is no yield curve, no pass-through coefficient and no product-specific beta. market_data rates are not used to reprice.

Time-weighted rate over the window

\[\text{profile} = \frac{r_0 D + (r_1 - r_0)(D - t_1)}{365}\]

This equals \(r_0 D/365\) until the first event, then \(r_1\) afterwards.

docs.title: 5. Balances
docs.text:
\[g = \begin{cases} 1 + \dfrac{loan\_growth}{100} & \text{loans} \\[2mm] \left(1+\dfrac{deposit\_growth}{100}\right)\left(1-\dfrac{runoff}{100}\right) & \text{deposits (not Funding)} \\[2mm] 1 & \text{other} \end{cases} \qquad g \ge 0\] \[s = 1 + \frac{shock\%}{100}\quad(\text{FX shock for FX positions, gold shock for gold, else }0)\] \[b_1 = b_0 \cdot g \cdot s\]

Run-off and deposit growth apply to Deposit positions only; Treasury-segment deposits are Funding and are not run off.

docs.title: 6. Interest and its decomposition
docs.text: \[I_{before} = b_0 \cdot \frac{r_0 D}{365}\] \[I_{rate\text{-}only} = b_0 \cdot \text{profile}\] \[I_{after} = b_1 \cdot \text{profile}\] Effect Formula Rate effect \(I_{rate\text{-}only} - I_{before}\) Volume effect \(I_{after} - I_{rate\text{-}only}\) (growth, run-off and FX/gold shock) Interest change \(I_{after} - I_{before}\) = rate + volume

docs.title: 7. NII, NIM, cost of funds
docs.text:
\[NII = (\text{loan interest} + \text{investment interest}) - (\text{deposit interest} + \text{funding interest})\] \[NIM\% = \frac{NII \cdot 365/H}{\text{Loans} + \text{Investments}} \times 100\] \[CoF\% = \frac{\text{Interest expense} \cdot 365/H}{\text{Deposits} + \text{Funding}} \times 100\] \[\text{Loan/Deposit \%} = \frac{\text{Loans}}{\text{Deposits}} \times 100\]

NIM and cost of funds are annualised; NII is for the horizon.

Repricing gap

\[\text{Gap} = \sum_{\text{loans, investments, has event}} b - \sum_{\text{deposits, funding, has event}} b\]

docs.title: 8. P&L and value components
docs.text:
Component Formula Sign ΔNII \(NII_{after} - NII_{before}\) + or − Credit cost Loans: \(b_1 \cdot c \cdot H/365\) with \(c = \dfrac{25\cdot \max(\Delta unemp,0) + 20\cdot \max(-\Delta gdp,0)}{10000}\) shown as negative FX / gold revaluation \(sign \cdot b_0 \cdot g \cdot (s-1)\), sign +1 for loans and investments, −1 for deposits and funding + or − Investment MTM \(-\,dur \cdot \Delta r \cdot b_1\) for investments that are not gold, with \(dur = \dfrac{\max(first-sim,0)}{365\,(1+r_0)}\) + or − \[\text{Total} = \Delta NII - \text{credit cost} + \text{revaluation} + \text{MTM}\]

Illustrative constants

The 25 bps (unemployment) and 20 bps (GDP) credit-cost sensitivities are fixed, transparent placeholders in config.py. They are not calibrated to the bank's loss history. Only an increase in unemployment and a fall in GDP create cost; favourable moves create no gain.

docs.title: 9. Liquidity metrics
docs.text:
cashflow_metrics runs twice: before with neutral parameters and after with the scenario.

Metric Definition CF Inflow / Outflow Cash flows dated from the simulation date to the horizon end, amounts shocked by FX or gold when the flow is in that basis Run-off outflow \(\dfrac{runoff}{100} \times \sum (b_0 \cdot s)\) over deposits, added to horizon outflow CF Net Cashflow Inflow − outflow CF HQLA Balance of investments flagged HQLA CF LCR % (headline) \(\dfrac{\text{HQLA}}{\text{Deposits}} \times 100\) with after-scenario balances LCR Net Outflow 30-day scheduled outflows + run-off + 15 % of (deposits + funding). Computed and exposed, not used in the headline

The headline LCR is a proxy

The dashboard LCR is HQLA divided by deposits. It is not the Basel LCR (HQLA over 30-day net stressed outflows), and the risk rule compares it with a 100 % threshold. Check the value on real data before presenting it. See Limitations.

docs.title: 10. Macro block
docs.text: The latest policy rate, inflation, unemployment and GDP observations are read from market_data, shown "before", and shown "after" as the observation plus the scenario shock. They feed the banner and the AI payload; apart from credit cost, they do not alter any KPI.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
A loan of EGP 1,000,000 at 12 %, floating, repricing quarterly, next repricing in 30 days, horizon 365 days, rate shock +2 pp, no other drivers.

  • \(D = 365\), \(t_1 = 30\), \(r_1 = 14\%\)
  • profile \(= (0.12 \cdot 365 + 0.02 \cdot 335)/365 = 0.13836\)
  • \(I_{before} = 120{,}000\), \(I_{after} = 138{,}356\)
  • Rate effect \(= +18{,}356\), volume effect \(= 0\)
  • Repricing fraction \(= 335/365 = 91.8\%\)

docs.title: Self-consistency
docs.text: The validation table in Analytics & Validation recomputes NII, NIM, cost of funds, total P&L and LCR from the position detail and compares them with the reported values.

docs.title: Changelog: v1 to v2.1
docs.text: Version 2.1.0, calculation engine 2.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Area v1 v2.1 Structure Seven modules Fourteen files, with one module per page and a shared UI layer Scenario modes Four older modes Base Case, Combined Stress, Individual Parameter, Free Type Drivers Rate shocks with pass-through parameters, yield-curve shifts, product-specific loan and deposit rate shocks Nine drivers: policy rate, FX, gold, deposit run-off, loan growth, deposit growth, inflation, unemployment, GDP Repricing Yield-curve driven Event-based on each position's repricing date, parallel shock Balance effects Rates mainly Loan and deposit growth and run-off change interest FX and gold Not modelled as shocks Revaluation effect and balance effect P&L NII focused Total P&L and value impact: ΔNII, credit cost, FX/gold revaluation, investment MTM Data access Table reads Two flat SQL views in EGP, with a LEFT JOIN fallback Persistence Several statements One transaction; 15 KPI rows and 5 risk rows per run Reports None PDF, PowerPoint, ZIP, Excel with formulas, CSV Validation Basic Independent recomputation table, PASS or FAIL AI Explanation Explanation saved to the run, free-text parsing with regex fallback Launcher Manual Run_App.bat

docs.title: Improvements
docs.text:
• Table names are matched case-insensitively (LOWER(table_name)), so behaviour is the same on Windows and Linux MySQL.
  • The connection is built with URL.create, so passwords with special characters work.
  • The SQLAlchemy engine is cached with st.cache_resource.
  • Persistence runs in a single transaction.
  • Loan and deposit growth now change interest, not just balances.
  • Driver attribution with an interaction term.
  • Maturity ladder, exposure tables and top-position sensitivity.
  • Risk rating with explicit reasons.
  • Reload button and a 120-second data cache.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• Pass-through parameters and yield-curve repricing.
  • Product-specific shocks such as the old loan and deposit rate shock fields.
  • The old four-mode scenario naming.

docs.title: Known issues carried into v2.1
docs.text: See Limitations & Roadmap for the full list, including the Excel mismatch, the AI panel writing during render, the wrong DOCS_BASE_URL, and the unwired documentation page.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
The application uses an existing MySQL 8 database named nbe_alm_simulation. REQUIRED_TABLES in config.py lists the seven tables, and connect_existing_database() stops with a clear message if any is missing. Table names are matched case-insensitively (LOWER(table_name)), so the code works on Windows and Linux servers alike.

Source of this page

The tables and views below are taken from the project's current schema dump (NBE_Data.sql, InnoDB, utf8mb4_unicode_ci) and checked against what the v2.1 code reads and writes.

docs.title: The two flat views
docs.text: The engine reads two views, not the raw tables. Both pick the latest rate per currency from market_data (ROW_NUMBER() ... ORDER BY as_of_datetime DESC, market_data_id DESC) and join the latest macro indicators.

docs.title: vw_alm_flat_table (one row per position, 33 columns)
docs.text:
Group Columns Identity Position_ID, Product_ID, Product_Code, Product_Name, Product_Type, Product_Family, Balance_Sheet_Side, ALM_Position_Category, Customer_Segment Valuation Currency, Valuation_Basis, Original_Balance_Or_Grams, Applied_Market_Rate, Evaluated_Balance_EGP Pricing Contractual_Interest_Rate, Rate_Type, Repricing_Frequency, Start_Date, Maturity_Date, Next_Repricing_Date Timing Remaining_Maturity_Days, Days_To_Next_Repricing (both measured from today's date, not the simulation date) Cash-flow summary Scheduled_Cashflows_Count, Expected_Inflows_EGP, Expected_Outflows_EGP, Next_Cashflow_Date, HQLA_Liquidity_Flag Macro CBE_Policy_Rate, Inflation_Rate, Real_Interest_Rate, Unemployment_Rate, GDP_Growth_Rate State Status

Rules inside the view:

  • Evaluated_Balance_EGP = ROUND(balance × latest rate for the position's currency, 2), with rate 1.0 when no rate is found.
  • Repricing_Frequency = the product's frequency, else Monthly for floating and At Maturity for fixed.
  • ALM_Position_Category is simply positions.position_type.
  • Product_Family is derived: Treasury Bills or Bonds → Sovereign Debt; gold → Precious Metals; credit cards or loans → Retail & Corp Lending; product type like Accounts → CASA (Current & Saving); everything else → Term Deposits & CDs.
  • HQLA_Liquidity_Flag is MAX(cash_flows.hqla_flag) for the position. A position with no cash flows is never HQLA.

docs.title: Fallback when a view is incomplete
docs.text: load_alm_data() compares len(view) with the row count of its source table. If equal and non-empty, the view is used. Otherwise an equivalent LEFT JOIN query (_LEFT_POS_SQL, _LEFT_CF_SQL) rebuilds the same columns, so positions whose product row is missing are not dropped, and a note says which path was used.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Item Convention Rates Decimal fractions. 0.12 is 12 %. Market values normalize_market_yield treats absolute values above 2 as percentages (18.5 becomes 0.185). Amounts EGP equivalents. Gold = grams × the latest gold price for currency XAU. Shock units pp for rates and macro, percent for FX, gold and balances policy_rate_shock_bps pp × 100 Categories loan, deposit, funding, investment, matched case-insensitively Row limit DB_READ_LIMIT = 100000 per table

Funding appears in two ways

The sample data stores two positions with position_type = 'Funding', and one Deposit in the Treasury segment. The engine treats all three as Funding (FUNDING_SEGMENTS = ["Treasury"]).

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[Run & save] --> B{Existing scenario?}
    B -- no --> C[INSERT scenarios<br/>code SCN-timestamp]
    B -- yes --> D[UPDATE scenarios]
    C --> E[INSERT simulation_runs<br/>executed_by = Streamlit]
    D --> E
    E --> F[INSERT simulation_results<br/>15 KPI rows + 5 RISK rows]
  • Everything runs in one engine.begin() block: all saved or nothing.
  • Inserts keep only columns that exist in the target table, so the code tolerates schema differences. The flip side: a misspelt column is skipped silently.
  • Each result row carries result_type, base and scenario values, absolute and percentage impact, unit, severity and direction.
  • simulation_runs.ai_explanation holds the AI narrative once generated.

docs.title: Design Decisions
docs.text: Each entry records what was chosen, why, and what it costs.

docs.title: 1. Deterministic engine, AI only explains
docs.text:
Decision. Every figure is computed by Python. The language model receives results and writes prose.

Why. ALM numbers must be reproducible and auditable. A model can mis-add or invent a figure.

Cost. Explanations are only as good as the small local model.

docs.title: 2. Local model (Ollama + Phi-3)
docs.text:
Decision. Run the model on the bank's machine.

Why. Position data should not leave the premises.

Cost. Lower language quality than hosted models, and slow on weak hardware (hence the 800-second timeout).

docs.title: 3. Existing database, no DDL
docs.text:
Decision. The application never creates or alters tables.

Why. The schema belongs to the data team; the app should not be able to damage it.

Cost. The app depends on the exact schema; missing tables stop it with a clear message.

docs.title: 4. Flat SQL views with Python fallback
docs.text:
Decision. Joins and EGP conversion live in two views. If a view's row count differs from its source, an embedded LEFT JOIN query is used.

Why. Keeps Python simple and ensures no position is dropped by an inner join.

Cost. The join logic exists twice and must stay in sync.

docs.title: 5. Everything converted to EGP in SQL
docs.text:
Decision. FX and gold balances are valued with the latest rate in the view; the engine works in one currency.

Why. Consistent totals and simple formulas.

Cost. Currency exposure is represented only through a shock factor, not a currency-level model.

docs.title: 6. Event-based repricing with a parallel shock
docs.text:
Decision. A rate shock applies after each position's first repricing event, in proportion to the time remaining.

Why. It reflects contract mechanics, so a one-year fixed loan and a daily-repricing deposit react differently.

Cost. No curve shape and no pass-through. See Limitations.

docs.title: 7. Rollover at maturity
docs.text:
Decision. Positions that mature in the window are assumed to renew and reprice at maturity; already matured positions are excluded.

Why. Keeps the balance sheet static over the horizon, which is the standard simplification for a gap-style analysis.

docs.title: 8. Treasury deposits are Funding
docs.text:
Decision. Deposits from the Treasury segment are classed as wholesale funding.

Why. They behave like market funding, not customer deposits, and should not be run off or counted in the customer deposit base.

docs.title: 9. Nine drivers that map one-to-one to database columns
docs.text:
Decision. PARAM_SPECS defines the drivers once; the UI, persistence, reports and parser all read it.

Why. Adding a driver is one entry plus the engine logic, and the saved scenario always matches what ran.

docs.title: 10. A driver-attribution table with an interaction row
docs.text:
Decision. Each driver is run alone and the residual is shown as Interaction.

Why. Management asks which factor caused this. The residual makes the table add up honestly instead of hiding combined effects.

docs.title: 11. Independent validation table
docs.text:
Decision. Headline KPIs are recomputed from the position detail and marked PASS or FAIL.

Why. Gives engineers a visible self-check.

Cost. It tests consistency of the summary, not correctness of the model.

docs.title: 12. Excel with live formulas
docs.text:
Decision. The Row-by-Row export contains formulas, not pasted values.

Why. Reviewers can trace each number in a tool they trust.

Cost. A second implementation of the maths. It can drift from the engine (see Limitations A).

docs.title: 13. Single transaction for persistence
docs.text:
Decision. Scenario, run and results are saved together.

Why. No half-saved runs.

docs.title: 14. Cache data for 120 seconds, engine without expiry
docs.text:
Decision. Tables are cached briefly; a Reload data button clears the cache.

Why. Streamlit reruns on every click; reading the database each time would be slow.

docs.title: 15. Documentation as code
docs.text:
Decision. These pages are Markdown in a repository, built with MkDocs Material and deployed to GitHub Pages.

Why. They are versioned with the project, reviewable, searchable and always one command from publishing.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Questions an engineering review is likely to raise, with direct answers.

docs.title: About the numbers
docs.text:
Does the AI calculate anything?

No. Every number comes from Python. The model reads the results and writes text, and the prompt forbids new numbers. See AI Assistant.

How is NII computed?

Per position: balance × rate × days ÷ 365 over the horizon, summed as (loan + investment interest) − (deposit + funding interest). See Calculation Engine.

Is NII annual or for the horizon?

For the horizon. NIM and cost of funds are annualised.

What happens to a rate shock on a fixed-rate loan?

Nothing until it matures. If it matures inside the horizon it is assumed to roll over and reprice at that date.

Why does a rate shock not change a position until some date?

The shock applies after the position's first repricing event, so the impact is proportional to the time left in the horizon.

Is there a yield curve or pass-through?

No. One parallel shift is applied. It is the main modelling limitation. See Limitations.

What does the Eligible column mean?

The position has a repricing event inside the horizon. It is not a flag for floating rate.

docs.title: About liquidity and risk
docs.text:
Is the LCR the Basel LCR?

No. The headline is HQLA ÷ deposits. The 30-day stressed outflow is computed but not used. The risk rule compares the proxy with 100 %.

Why does deposit run-off improve my results?

Deposits leaving reduce interest expense and shrink the deposit base used in the LCR proxy, and the model does not charge a replacement funding cost. This is a known limitation, not a feature.

Why is the rating HIGH on the base case?

The proxy is below the 100 % limit, so the rule returns HIGH. On the sample database the base case shows LCR 79.5 % and overall risk HIGH. The rating then says little about the scenario itself.

What does inflation do?

Nothing to the KPIs. It is stored, shown, and passed to the AI.

docs.title: About the data
docs.text:
Which database does it need?

MySQL 8 with seven tables and two views. It never creates objects. See Database.

Why two SQL views?

They join products and market rates and convert everything to EGP, so Python receives one clean row per position and per cash flow.

What if a view is out of date?

The loader compares its row count with the source table. If they differ, it uses an equivalent query and shows a note.

How fresh is the data?

Cached for 120 seconds. Reload data forces a refresh.

docs.title: About use
docs.text:
Can I compare scenarios?

Yes. Saved scenarios can be compared on the Scenarios page, and the dashboard attribution table compares drivers inside one scenario.

Can I rerun a saved scenario with new data?

Yes, with run mode Rerun Saved Scenario, or by selecting it on the dashboard, which re-evaluates it on current data.

How do I describe a scenario in words?

Use Free Type Scenario, for example Interest rates +300 bps; USD/EGP +15%; deposit outflows 10%. Check the extracted table before running.

Why does the Excel not match the screen?

It uses its own formulas. In edge cases (blank or past repricing dates, rollover) it can differ. The engine is the reference. See Reports.

Is it ready for production?

It is a prototype. Authentication, tests, a Basel-style LCR and a yield curve would be the main steps. See the roadmap in Limitations.

Is this an official NBE application?

No. It carries an NBE-inspired theme, and any use of the NBE name and logo needs the bank's permission.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Item Notes Python 3.10+ The code uses tuple[bool, str]-style typing and f-strings with nested quotes. MySQL 8 With the ALM database loaded (default name nbe_alm_simulation). Ollama + Phi-3 Optional. Needed only for AI explanations and AI parsing of free-text scenarios.

Python packages, inferred from the imports:

pip install streamlit pandas numpy plotly sqlalchemy pymysql requests openpyxl
pip install reportlab python-pptx kaleido      # only for PDF / PPTX export

The report libraries are optional: without them the dashboard shows a hint instead of the export form.

docs.title: 1. Prepare the database
docs.text:
The application connects to an existing database and never creates tables. Besides the seven tables it expects two SQL views that flatten positions and cash flows into EGP-valued rows:

Object Type Purpose products, positions, cash_flows, market_data tables Source data scenarios, simulation_runs, simulation_results tables Saved scenarios, runs and KPI results vw_alm_flat_table view One row per position, valued in EGP vw_alm_cashflows_flat view One row per cash flow, valued in EGP

If a view is missing or incomplete

The loader compares the view's row count with the raw table. If they differ, it falls back to an equivalent LEFT JOIN query embedded in database.py, so no position is silently dropped. See Database.

docs.title: 2. Configure
docs.text:
Settings come from environment variables, with defaults in config.py.

Variable Default Purpose DB_HOST localhost MySQL host DB_PORT 3306 MySQL port DB_NAME nbe_alm_simulation Database DB_USER root User DB_PASSWORD (empty) Password DB_DRIVER mysql+pymysql SQLAlchemy driver OLLAMA_HOST http://localhost:11434 Ollama endpoint OLLAMA_MODEL phi3 Model name OLLAMA_TIMEOUT 800 Seconds per request OLLAMA_TEMPERATURE 0.0 Sampling temperature for explanations DATA_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS 120 (constant) How long loaded data is cached

Development defaults

root with an empty password is for local development only. Use a dedicated least-privilege account anywhere else. See Security.

The connection values can also be edited at run time in Data & Settings → Database connection.

docs.title: 3. Logo files (optional)
docs.text:
The interface and reports look for these images in the folder where the app is started. If a file is missing, the logo is skipped silently.

File Used for nbe_logo_only.png Sidebar icon nbe_logo_w.png Header banner and PowerPoint header (white version) nbe_logo.png PDF report header

docs.title: 4. Run
docs.text:
Windows shortcutCommand line

Double-click Run_App.bat. It starts Streamlit without a console window:

@echo off
cd /d "%~dp0"
start "" pythonw -m streamlit run app.py
exit

streamlit run app.py

If the connection fails the app does not stop. Open Data & Settings → Database connection, where the real MySQL error is shown, fix the values and press Save and reconnect.

docs.title: 5. Optional: local AI
docs.text:
ollama pull phi3
ollama serve

Without Ollama, free-text scenarios fall back to regex parsing, and the explanation panel shows a message that the model is unavailable.

docs.title: 6. First run in three steps
docs.text:
1. Scenarios → Create & run. Pick Combined Stress Scenario, set values, press Run & save simulation.
  2. Dashboard. Read the KPI cards, the management insight and the risk badge, then explore the tabs.
  3. Explain this scenario. Ask the local AI for an executive explanation, then export a report if needed.

docs.title: Limitations & Roadmap
docs.text: This page lists what the model does not do and the defects found while documenting v2.1. They come from reading the code and from running the real engine on a synthetic portfolio, so each item can be reproduced.

docs.title: Modelling scope
docs.text: # Limitation Consequence 1 Parallel rate shock only. One shift applied to every position after its first repricing event. No yield curve, no product-specific pass-through, no beta Cannot show that deposit rates lag market rates or that a steepening curve affects products differently 2 market_data rates do not reprice anything. It is used for FX and gold valuation and the macro snapshot Rate scenarios are independent of the observed curve 3 Balance changes are not funded. Loan growth adds interest income with no matching funding cost; deposit growth is not invested Growth scenarios look favourable to NII 4 Run-off improves NII and the LCR proxy. Deposits leave, so interest expense falls, and a smaller deposit base raises HQLA ÷ deposits The sign is the opposite of a real run-off stress. In the verification portfolio, adding run-off raised NII and the proxy 5 LCR is a proxy. Headline value is HQLA ÷ deposits, compared with a 100 % limit. The 30-day stressed outflow denominator is computed but not used Rates every scenario HIGH. Confirmed on the sample database: the base case shows LCR 79.5 % and overall risk HIGH (see the screenshot in User Interface) 6 Inflation has no KPI effect Setting it changes nothing except the stored value, the macro banner and the AI payload 7 Macro shocks act only through credit cost, with fixed 25 / 20 bps constants, one-sided (only adverse moves cost) Illustrative, not calibrated 8 Credit cost is only on loans and is a flat rate on the stressed balance No segment, stage or collateral detail 9 Rollover assumption. Positions maturing inside the window are assumed to roll at the same balance and reprice at maturity No new-business volume or margin assumption 10 Single horizon, no dynamic balance sheet No multi-period projection 11 Pre-tax, no fees or non-interest income, no capital or leverage Not a full earnings forecast 12 Investment MTM uses a simple duration from the first repricing event Convexity and credit spreads ignored

docs.title: Defects and risks found in v2.1
docs.text: # Finding Where Impact A Excel export can disagree with the engine. A fixed-rate loan rolling at maturity showed a repricing fraction of 100 % in Excel and 66.85 % in the engine, about 5.2 M EGP of interest on one position. Blank or past repricing dates are the sensitive case export_row_by_row_with_formulas_xlsx A reviewer recalculating in Excel may not match the dashboard B AI panel writes to the database while rendering. If no run is found for a scenario name, it inserts a scenario and a run render_ai_scenario_panel Opening a dashboard can create rows; runs are matched by name, so duplicate names collide C String-built SQL with only single quotes doubled AI panel, report builder Backslash sequences can break the query; use bound parameters D DOCS_BASE_URL points to another account, amr-khaled-abdelfatach.github.io/NBE_ALM/ config.py, ui.py The sidebar Documentation button opens a different site E page_documentation.py is broken and unused. It imports effective_drivers and doc_button, which no longer exist page_documentation.py Importing it fails F Hard-coded market values. USD/EGP 48.613 and gold 4220.42 are typed into the dashboard banner. They equal the latest rows in the current dump (17 Oct 2026) page_dashboard.py Correct today, but the banner will go stale as soon as market_data is updated G Debug line Current Run ID: … is shown in the AI panel. In the dark theme the sidebar Documentation link button is nearly unreadable (dark text on a dark button) ui_common.py, ui.py Cosmetic H Duplicate report-builder code. An inline copy runs; a @st.fragment copy (render_report_builder_section) is never called page_dashboard.py Maintenance risk I Silent column dropping. Inserts keep only columns that exist persist_simulation A schema typo loses data without an error J No authentication. Every run is stored with executed_by = "Streamlit" database.py No audit trail of who ran what K No automated tests and few docstrings; from config import * hides origins of names all modules Harder review and safer refactoring is needed L Commented-out code and unused settings, for example the data-quality tab and several unused config values various Noise

docs.title: Interpretation notes
docs.text:
• The column Eligible means has a repricing event inside the horizon.
  • NII is for the horizon; NIM and cost of funds are annualised.
  • The validation table checks internal consistency, not reconciliation to the ledger.
  • The SQL dump supplied with the project is the older schema. The v2.1 structure documented here is derived from the code.

docs.title: Suggested roadmap
docs.text:
Quick fixesModellingPlatform
  1. Point DOCS_BASE_URL to this site.
  2. Replace string-built SQL with bound parameters.
  3. Stop the AI panel from inserting rows; save runs only on Run & save.
  4. Remove the debug line, dead code and the broken page, or fix it.
  5. Read FX and gold for the banner from market_data.
  6. Align the Excel formulas with the engine's rollover rule, and add a test that compares them.
  1. Replace the HQLA ÷ deposits proxy with a Basel-style LCR (HQLA over 30-day net stressed outflows) and calibrate the limit.
  2. Make run-off an outflow with a funding replacement cost.
  3. Add a yield curve and product pass-through betas.
  4. Fund balance growth, and add new-business margins.
  5. Calibrate the credit-cost constants and make them two-sided.
  6. Give inflation a defined channel or remove the driver.
  1. User login and executed_by from the session.
  2. Unit tests for the engine with golden cases, plus CI.
  3. Role-based access to saved scenarios and reports.
  4. Scheduled runs and approval workflow for ALCO packs.

docs.title: Executive report builder
docs.text:
The form lets the analyst choose:

  1. KPIs. Up to nine cards: NII, NIM, cost of funds, total P&L and value impact, LCR, net cash flow, total loans, total deposits. The first six are pre-selected.
  2. Charts. NII bridge, P&L components, portfolio before vs after, and balance by currency when available.
  3. Include comparison table and Include management / AI insight.
  4. Output format. PDF, PPTX, or both.

Charts are rendered to PNG by Kaleido (plotly_fig_to_png_bytes) and embedded.

docs.title: What goes into each file
docs.text:
PDF (landscape A4)PowerPointZIP bundle
  1. Title, scenario type, date and horizon
  2. Active scenario parameters, shown as chips
  3. Scenario explanation and management insight
  4. Selected KPI table (before, after, change)
  5. Selected charts
  6. Full comparison table
  7. Header and footer on every page
  1. Title slide
  2. Parameters slide
  3. KPI slide
  4. AI or management insight slide
  5. One slide per selected chart
  6. NBE-style header and footer on every slide

Choosing Both produces a ZIP containing the PDF and the PPTX with the same base name, plus buttons to download either one alone.

File names follow NBE_ALM_Report_<scenario>_<yyyymmdd>.

docs.title: Where the explanation text comes from
docs.text:
The report never starts the AI. It looks, in order, for:

  1. the explanation already shown on the dashboard in this session,
  2. the explanation saved on the run in simulation_runs.ai_explanation,
  3. otherwise the deterministic management insight sentences.

So a report is always reproducible and never blocks waiting for the model. Generate the AI explanation first if you want it in the report.

Header logo

The report header uses the logo files named in Getting Started when they are present next to the app.

docs.title: Row-by-Row Excel
docs.text:
build_full_row_by_row_scenario_table joins each position's inputs, the scenario parameters and the isolated effects. export_row_by_row_with_formulas_xlsx then writes the table to Excel with live formulas for interest, effects and totals, so a reviewer can change a cell and see the result recalculate.

Excel can differ from the dashboard in edge cases

The workbook recomputes interest from the repricing date and frequency columns with its own formulas. While verifying this documentation against a synthetic portfolio, the Excel and the engine disagreed for a fixed-rate loan that rolls over at maturity: the engine gave a repricing fraction of 66.85 %, the workbook 100 %, a difference of about 5.2 million EGP of interest on that one position. Positions with a blank or already-past repricing date are the sensitive case. Treat the dashboard (engine) numbers as the reference and use the workbook to inspect structure. See Limitations.

docs.title: Checking a report
docs.text: Before circulating a report, compare its KPI table with the Calculation audit tab (Data & Settings). All rows should read PASS.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text: A scenario is a set of up to nine numeric drivers, a simulation date and a horizon. The same nine drivers are the nine numeric columns of the scenarios table, so what you run is exactly what is saved.

docs.title: The nine drivers
docs.text:
Defined once in PARAM_SPECS (config.py). The UI, the database mapping, the reports and the free-text parser all read this table.

Key Label Unit Allowed range Step Group rate_change_pp Policy / market rate shock pp −1000 to 1000 0.25 Market fx_shock_pct FX shock (USD/EGP & FCY) % −500 to 500 1 Market gold_shock_pct Gold price shock % −500 to 500 1 Market deposit_runoff_pct Deposit run-off (outflow) % 0 to 100 1 Balance sheet & liquidity loan_growth_pct Loan growth % −100 to 100 1 Balance sheet & liquidity deposit_growth_pct Deposit growth % 0 to 100 1 Balance sheet & liquidity inflation_shock_pct Inflation shock pp −200 to 200 0.5 Macro unemployment_shock_pct Unemployment shock pp −100 to 100 0.5 Macro gdp_shock_pct GDP growth shock pp −200 to 200 0.5 Macro

All defaults are 0, which is the base case. The UI clamps every input to its range.

Inflation has no KPI effect

inflation_shock_pct is stored, shown in the macro snapshot and passed to the AI, but no formula in the engine uses it. See Limitations.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Template scenario_type Behaviour Base Case BASE No assumptions. Before and after are equal. Combined Stress Scenario COMBINED_STRESS All nine drivers are visible, grouped in three sections. Values start at zero. Individual Parameter Scenario INDIVIDUAL_PARAMETER Choose one driver, set one value, all others stay neutral. Free Type Scenario FREE_TYPE Describe the scenario in words. Numbers are extracted by Phi-3 or by regex.

resolve_saved_template maps a saved row back to a template, and build_saved_template_values rebuilds the form values, so a saved scenario reopens in the same shape it was created in.

docs.title: Simulation window
docs.text: Setting Default Notes Simulation date today The horizon is counted from this date. Horizon 365 days 1 to 3650. Presets: 30, 90, 180, 365, 730. Run mode New Scenario Rerun Saved Scenario loads a saved scenario's values into the form.

docs.title: Unit conversions
docs.text: Where Rule Engine rate shock rate_change_pp / 100 is added to a decimal rate. +3 pp is +0.03. Database policy_rate_shock_bps = rate_change_pp × 100. A +3 pp shock is stored as 300. Free text 300 bps, +3% and 3 pp all become rate_change_pp = 3.

docs.title: Free-text scenarios
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[Text box] --> B[Extract assumptions]
    B --> C{Ollama running and<br/>model installed?}
    C -- yes --> D[Phi-3 returns JSON, temperature 0]
    C -- no --> E[Regex parser only]
    D --> F[Regex fills keys the model left empty]
    E --> G[Parameter table shown to the user]
    F --> G
    G --> H[Run & save]

Example input:

Interest rates +300 bps; USD/EGP +15%; gold price -10%; deposit outflows 10%.

The regex parser understands English and Arabic keywords (for example الدولار, الذهب, سحوبات, فائدة), units %, pp, bps, and decrease words such as drop, cut, انخفاض. Deposit run-off is always stored as a positive number. The extracted values are shown in a table before anything runs, so the user can check them.

docs.title: From the screen to the database
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant P as page_scenarios
    participant S as scenarios.py
    participant E as Engine
    participant D as database.py
    U->>P: choose template, set drivers
    P->>S: build_scenario_parameters(values)
    S-->>P: nine parameters, defaults filled
    U->>P: Run & save simulation

Reruns of a saved scenario reuse its scenario_id and update the row, then add a new simulation_runs record.

docs.title: Security & Data Handling
docs.text: This is a prototype. The table below states what is protected, what is not, and what to change before production use.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[Analyst browser] --> S[Streamlit process]
    S --> M[(MySQL)]
    S -. localhost .-> O[Ollama / Phi-3]
    S --> F[Reports in memory<br/>downloaded by the browser]

No external API is called. The AI runs on the same machine, and reports are built in memory and handed to the browser.

docs.title: Status of controls
docs.text: Area Status in v2.1 Recommendation Authentication None. Anyone who can open the URL can run scenarios Put the app behind the bank's SSO or reverse proxy Authorisation None Roles for viewing, running and saving Audit Runs stored with executed_by = "Streamlit" Record the real user DB account Defaults to root with an empty password Dedicated account: SELECT on tables and views, INSERT/UPDATE on scenarios, simulation_runs, simulation_results only Secrets Environment variables, or typed into the settings tab and kept in session_state Use a secrets manager; never commit credentials Password escaping Handled: connection built with URL.create Keep Transport Streamlit serves plain HTTP TLS at a reverse proxy SQL injection Reads and writes use SQLAlchemy parameters, but the AI panel and report builder build two queries by string and only double single quotes Replace with bound parameters Writes Single transaction; DDL is never executed Keep AI data egress None; Ollama is local Keep it local, or get approval for any hosted model Error display The real MySQL error is shown in the connection tab Hide details outside admin users HTML injection unsafe_allow_html is used for the logo and the CSS only, with fixed content Keep user text out of those blocks Reports May contain balances and scenario results Classify and store according to bank policy

docs.title: Data classification
docs.text: The application reads balances, rates and cash flows by position. Treat exports (Excel, CSV, PDF, PPTX) as confidential. They carry no password protection and no watermark in v2.1.

docs.title: Hardening checklist
docs.text:
1. Create a least-privilege MySQL user and set DB_USER and DB_PASSWORD.
  2. Run behind HTTPS and authentication.
  3. Change the default DOCS_BASE_URL.
  4. Fix the string-built SQL.
  5. Store the authenticated user in executed_by.
  6. Restrict who can reach the Data explorer, which shows every table.
  7. Add the license and disclosure text required for use of the NBE name and logo.

docs.title: User Interface
docs.text:
The application has three pages, reached from the sidebar. Every page is a function that receives the shared context built by ui.py.

Sidebar item Module Purpose Dashboard page_dashboard.py Results of the active scenario: KPIs, charts, tables, AI explanation, report export Scenarios page_scenarios.py Create and run, browse saved scenarios, compare scenarios Data & Settings page_system.py Data explorer, calculation audit, database and AI settings Documentation external link Opens DOCS_URL in a new tab Reload data button Clears the data cache and reruns

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
Base case on the sample database: header banner, scenario selector, FX and gold chips, risk badge and the first KPI cards.

The dashboard shows one scenario at a time. A selector at the top lets you switch between the scenario you just ran in this session and saved scenarios from the database (a saved scenario is re-evaluated on the fly with the current data).

docs.title: Header area
docs.text:
• KPI cards: NII, NIM, cost of funds, total P&L and value impact, LCR, net cash flow and the main balances, each with the change versus the base case. Colour tone follows whether higher is better for that metric.
  • Risk badge: the overall rating (LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH) from overall_risk_rating. See Analytics & Validation.
  • Driver chips: the drivers that are non-zero in the active scenario.
  • Management insight: short rule-based sentences from management_insights, produced without AI.

docs.title: Main tabs
docs.text: Tab Content 1. Overview NII bridge, P&L components chart, driver attribution table (standalone vs combined), KPI comparison table, AI explanation panel 2. Balances Portfolio before vs after (loans, deposits, funding, investments) and balance by currency 3. Liquidity Stressed maturity ladder: inflow, outflow and cumulative net by bucket

docs.title: Report builder
docs.text: An expander, Export Custom Executive Report, lets you pick KPIs, charts, whether to include the comparison table and the AI or management text, and the format (PDF, PPTX or both). See Reports & Exports.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text: Three tabs.

docs.title: Create & run
docs.text:
1. Template: Base Case, Combined Stress Scenario, Individual Parameter Scenario or Free Type Scenario.
  2. Simulation window: simulation date, horizon in days (1 to 3650), run mode (New Scenario or Rerun Saved Scenario), and quick presets for 30, 90, 180, 365 and 730 days.
  3. Assumptions: the nine drivers as number inputs, clamped to their allowed ranges. Individual mode shows one driver selector and one value. Free Type shows a text box and an Extract assumptions button.
  4. Run & save simulation. The scenario is evaluated and written to the database in one transaction.

Details are in Scenarios.

docs.title: Saved scenarios
docs.text: A table of all saved scenarios, and for the chosen one its stored assumptions with units.

docs.title: Compare scenarios
docs.text: Select several saved scenarios. The page takes the latest run of each, pivots the KPI results by metric, and charts the amount KPIs side by side. Nothing is selected by default.

Where the data-quality tab went

docs.title: Visual theme
docs.text: ui_common.py holds one large CSS block that applies an NBE-inspired palette (green, dark green, orange), card styles for KPIs, the risk badge and section headers. style_nbe_figure applies the same palette to every Plotly chart so charts, tables and exports look consistent.
